title: Kingdom of Numidia
summary: Numidia was a North African kingdom formed when the Massylian prince Masinissa, backed by Rome, defeated the Masaesylian king Syphax and united the two Numidian peoples. Its kings ruled from Cirta (modern Constantine) until Rome absorbed it between 46 and 40 BCE.

uncertainty.note: Start is the unification after Zama (202 BCE); Syphax was defeated at Cirta in 203 BCE. End: the source gives both Caesar's annexation after Thapsus (46 BCE) and the death of the last king Arabio (40 BCE).

where.modern_name: Constantine (ancient Cirta), Algeria; the kingdom extended across much of northern Algeria and Tunisia
where.historical_name: Cirta, capital of the Kingdom of Numidia

importance.justification: A Rome-allied North African kingdom that shaped the Punic Wars settlement and later the Jugurthine War, before becoming a Roman province.

sources.title: The Masaesyli and Massylii of Numidia
sources.author: Joshua J. Mark

reviewer_note: Least sure of the end date: 46 BCE (division under Caesar) versus 40 BCE (death of Arabio); the range covers both. Coordinates are modern Constantine (Cirta), the capital, not the whole kingdom. Wikidata was read only for the coordinate.
